title: Probabilistic user-pattern generator for multi-tenant streaming load
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a scalable, probabilistic load harness that simulates realistic multi-tenant streaming chat traffic (SSE + WebSocket) to measure tokens/sec, p95 latencies, and detect regressions. The harness should support stochastic session lengths, variable token pacing, KV-cache warm/cold scenarios, prefix reuse, and dynamic concurrency shaping to reproduce production mixes. It will run in both synthetic and replay modes and feed metrics into our regression detector and Grafana alerting pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can spawn 50k concurrent streaming sessions (mix of SSE and WebSocket) across simulated tenants
Produces token-level throughput and latency metrics (tokens/sec, p50/p90/p95/p99) per tenant and global
KV-cache awareness: can simulate cold/warm KV cache hit rates and report impact on p95
Supports deterministic replay mode using recorded session traces and a stochastic synthetic mode driven by user distributions
Integrates with regression detector and emits dataset snapshot + baseline comparison for automated gating
Expose configuration for concurrency shaping (step, linear, poisson), token pacing, prompt diversity, and model variant fallbacks
Produces artifacts: load report JSON, Grafana dashboard link, and CI-friendly regression summary
work_items: Design probabilistic session model (session length dist, inter-token delay, message size distribution)
Implement SSE and WebSocket client pools with connection churn controls
Add KV-cache simulator hooks to mark requests as cold/warm and measure KV lookup latency impact
Metric plumbing: per-token timing, per-session p95, aggregated tokens/sec, label by tenant/model/route
Regression integration: snapshot current run -> compare to baseline -> post summary to CI and alerts
Create synthetic user-mix presets (small-startup, enterprise-burst, plateau-heavy) for reuse
Docs + runbook for running large-scale experiments on dedicated CI runners or k8s job clusters
risks: Load generator itself may become bottleneck — need horizontal sharding and efficient token emulation (avoid heavy JSON parsing per token)
Network egress and ephemeral port exhaustion when simulating high concurrent WS/SSE connections
False positives in regression detector if baseline isn't representative; need warm-up and controlled baseline selection
KV-cache simulation must be accurate; naive models could under/over-estimate p95 impact
notes: We should prefer a single binary written in Rust for low footprint; prototype in Go acceptable for faster iteration.
Will reuse existing session-replay traces from ENG-61123 and ENG-24680 but transform them into probabilistic distributions rather than exact replays.
Plan to add a lightweight local mode for devs to run small-scale smoke tests before scheduling large cluster runs.
Consider exporting an 'experiment manifest' (json) that captures seed, mix, and config for reproducibility in CI

2026-02-28 Marco Chen: KV-cache hooks added. Observed 2x p95 increase in synthetic cold-warm transitions in local run. Created grafana dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/stream-load/probabilistic-harness

2026-03-01 Aisha Patel: Integration plan for regression detector drafted. Will snapshot token-level latency histograms and post results to CI. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1098
release_notes: Adds a scalable probabilistic streaming load harness that models tenant mixes, token pacing, and KV cache effects. Intended for runtime-2.4 regression gating and capacity planning.
run_instructions: 1) Checkout runtime/probes/probabilistic-harness; 2) Build with make -C probes; 3) Create experiment manifest; 4) kubectl apply -f job.yaml --namespace load-tests; 5) Monitor Grafana and wait for snapshot artifact in /tmp/harness-runs/<id>.json
observability: Emits prom labels: experiment, tenant, model, route, session_id. Histograms: token_latency_seconds (p50/p90/p95/p99), gauge: tokens_per_sec, counter: tokens_emitted_total
final_decision: Proceed with Rust-based generator for performance-critical path; provide Go shim for quick experiments. Baseline run will be required before gating any CI jobs.
